replies.text: What's a good book on management for first-time leads?
replies.reply: For first-time leads—especially in engineering—*The Manager's Path* by Camille Fournier is the standard recommendation; it walks through each transition from individual contributor to senior leader. If you want something shorter and more general, *The First-Time Manager* or Kim Scott's *Radical Candor* (on giving feedback and earning trust) are good complements. If it's Tomas asking, Fournier's book is the best fit given his role leading Helix's engineering team through the Atlas migration.

replies.reply: Great — noted! replies.text: New blocker: Sara says the Dagster deployment on our Kubernetes cluster needs a bigger node pool, approval pending from finance.
replies.reply: Noted: a new Atlas-migration blocker — per Sara (SRE), the Dagster deployment on the Kubernetes cluster needs a bigger node pool, and the request is pending finance approval.

replies.text: Do you have a recipe for a quick weeknight pasta?
replies.reply: Absolutely — try this garlicky lemon one-pot pasta: cook spaghetti until al dente (reserve a cup of pasta water). Meanwhile, sauté sliced garlic in olive oil with a pinch of red pepper flakes, toss in the pasta with the pasta water, a squeeze of lemon, handful of parmesan, and any quick greens (spinach or frozen peas). Total time ~20 minutes. Want a version with protein like canned tuna or sausage?

replies.text: Any idea why my standing desk keeps drifting down?
replies.reply: Common culprits: a failing gas strut or low-pressure spring (pneumatic desks), a too-tight touch-sensitive control panel that drops the height when bumped, or a loose/wrong wired keypad committing accidental adjustments. Also heavy sustained loads (e.g., triple monitors) can outpace the lift. If it's a manual/crank desk, the locking nut may be slipping. For electronic desks, try resetting the controller (often holding a button for several seconds) — if it still drifts, the control box or strut likely needs replacing.

replies.reply: Nice — with the node pool in place, Dagster is now in staging. That's a key Atlas milestone done; next up are validating the DAGs/cost targets in staging and prepping for the prod cutover.
